title: DelegationTokenPayload.from_cbor missing type validation
description:
In delegation_tokens.py, from_cbor() does not type-check fields after CBOR decoding.

Impact: If delegate is a string instead of bytes, it passes len() validation but silently fails during IID comparison (returns 'DELEGATE_MISMATCH' instead of a type error). Similar issues exist for scope, resource, expiry, and seq fields.

File: python/src/lichen/crypto/delegation_tokens.py
Function: DelegationTokenPayload.from_cbor() (line 158)

Fix: Add explicit type checks for each field:
- delegate: isinstance(v, bytes)
- scope: isinstance(v, int)
- resource: isinstance(v, str)
- expiry: isinstance(v, int)
- seq: isinstance(v, int)
close_reason: DelegationTokenPayload.from_cbor (python/src/lichen/crypto/delegation_tokens.py:157-194) now fail-closes the CBOR trust boundary: requires the decoded payload to be a dict and exact-type-checks every field (bytes delegate, int scope/expiry/seq, str resource) raising TypeError before dataclass construction. Rationale: __post_init__ length/range validation alone let wrong types through (str delegate of len 8 passed len() and later failed as DELEGATE_MISMATCH instead of a type error); type-exact checks (not isinstance) also reject bool for int fields. Added TestFromCborTypeValidation: valid round trip, non-map rejection, and 8 wrong-type field cases (bytearray case excluded — cbor2 normalizes bytearray to bytes on the wire, unobservable at this boundary). Missing-field KeyError behavior unchanged/documented. crypto vector suite: 88 passed; ruff clean; 0 mypy errors in delegation_tokens.py (2 pre-existing in an imported file). 3x codereview via reviewer model (kimi-k3): correctness PASS (nits non-blocking), security no findings, edge-cases PASS.
